definitions.gloss: seven spring herbs; seven herbs of spring
definitions.explanation: A set of seven edible wild herbs traditionally eaten in a rice porridge on January 7th. The seven herbs are: seri (water dropwort), nazuna (shepherd's purse), gogyo (cudweed), hakobera (chickweed), hotokenoza (henbit), suzuna (turnip), and suzushiro (daikon radish).

examples.japanese: ⟦{一月|いちがつ}→一月：00631_ichigatsu⟧⟦{七日|なのか}→七日：02927_nanoka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{春|はる}の{七草|ななくさ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: We eat the seven spring herbs on January 7th.

examples.japanese: ⟦スーパー→スーパー：01061_suupaa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{春|はる}の{七草|ななくさ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦セット→セット：03853_setto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}って→買う：00489_kau⟧きた。
examples.english: I bought a set of seven spring herbs at the supermarket.

examples.english: I made seven-herb porridge with the spring herbs to rest my stomach, which was tired from overeating during New Year's.

notes:
A deeply rooted New Year tradition in Japan. On January 7th ({人日|じんじつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{節句|せっく}→節句：26925_sekku⟧), families prepare ⟦{七草粥|ななくさがゆ}→七草粥：22751_nanakusagayu⟧ (seven-herb rice porridge) using these seven herbs. The custom is believed to ward off illness, bring good fortune for the year, and give the stomach a rest after rich New Year foods.

THE SEVEN HERBS:
- {芹|せり}: water dropwort
- {薺|なずな}: shepherd's purse
- {御形|ごぎょう}: cudweed
- {繁縷|はこべら}: chickweed
- {仏の座|ほとけのざ}: henbit
- {菘|すずな}: turnip
- {蘿蔔|すずしろ}: daikon radish

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{七草粥|ななくさがゆ}→七草粥：22751_nanakusagayu⟧: seven-herb rice porridge
- ⟦{七草|ななくさ}→七草：11190_nanakusa⟧⟦セット→セット：03853_setto⟧: seven-herb set (sold at supermarkets in early January)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Supermarkets across Japan sell pre-packaged sets of the seven herbs every January. There is also ⟦{秋|あき}→秋：02276_aki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{七草|ななくさ}→七草：11190_nanakusa⟧ (seven autumn herbs), but those are traditionally for viewing, not eating.
